# njoagleod

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/tor-gu/njoagleod/workflows/R-CMD-check/badge.svg)](https://github.com/tor-gu/njoagleod/actions)
<!-- badges: end -->

This is a cleaned-up version of the NJ OAG Law Enforcement Officer Diversity
  database available from https://www.njoag.gov/policerecruiting/

## Dataset Overview
This package is built from the 2025 NJ OAG release, which covers officers for
2021--2025 and agencies and applicants for 2022--2025. It contains six tables.

* ```agency``` One row per law enforcement agency (per name, if the agency is renamed).
  Each agency has a stable ```agency_id```.
* ```agency_alias``` Every spelling of every agency's name, in the NJ OAG releases and in
  the [```njoaguof```](https://github.com/tor-gu/njoaguof) package, mapped to its
  ```agency_id```.
* ```agency_municipality``` The municipalities each agency serves, identified as in the
  [```njmunicipalities```](https://github.com/tor-gu/njmunicipalities) package.
* ```agency_practice``` Each agency's hiring and promotion practices, by year.
* ```officer``` Counts of officers by year, agency, race, age range, gender and promotion.
* ```applicant``` Counts of applicants by year, agency, race, age range, gender, applicant
  type and outcome.

## Examples
```{r, message = FALSE}
library(njoagleod)
library(dplyr)
```

The ```agency``` table looks like this:
```{r}
agency
```
The columns ```agency_id``` and ```first_year``` form the primary key. The other tables
refer to agencies by ```agency_id``` only.

The ```officer``` and ```applicant``` tables are count tables: each row is a combination of
characteristics, and ```officer_count``` (or ```applicant_count```) is the number of people
who share it.
```{r}
officer
```
So count people with the count as a weight. Counting rows counts combinations, not officers.
```{r}
officer %>%
  filter(year == 2025) %>%
  count(officer_race, wt = officer_count, name = "officers")
```

To attach agency names to a table, join ```agency``` on the ```agency_id``` and the
years each name was in use:
```{r}
officer %>%
  count(year, agency_id, wt = officer_count, name = "officers") %>%
  left_join(agency, join_by(agency_id, between(year, first_year, final_year))) %>%
  select(year, agency_county, agency_name, officers) %>%
  arrange(desc(officers))
```

### Municipalities
```agency_municipality``` identifies municipalities by ```GEOID_Y2K```, the stable municipality
identifier of the ```njmunicipalities``` package. It does not change when a municipality
is renamed or assigned a new GEOID. To get the name and GEOID in effect in a given year:
```{r}
agency_municipality %>%
  left_join(
    njmunicipalities::get_municipalities(2025, geoid_year = 2000,
                                         geoid_ref_as_ref_column = TRUE),
    by = c("GEOID_Y2K" = "GEOID_ref")
  ) %>%
  left_join(agency %>% filter(first_year <= 2025, final_year >= 2025), by = "agency_id") %>%
  select(agency_name, GEOID, county, municipality)
```
Agencies that serve more than one municipality have one row for each:
```{r}
agency %>%
  filter(agency_type == "Multiple Municipalities") %>%
  inner_join(agency_municipality, by = "agency_id") %>%
  left_join(
    njmunicipalities::get_municipalities(2025, geoid_year = 2000,
                                         geoid_ref_as_ref_column = TRUE),
    by = c("GEOID_Y2K" = "GEOID_ref")
  ) %>%
  select(agency_name, municipality)
```

### Use with ```njoaguof```
```agency_alias``` maps the agency names used by ```njoaguof``` to ```agency_id```. For
example, here are the agencies with the most use-of-force incidents per officer in 2024.
(See the note below on incomplete agency reports.)
```{r}
uof_agency <- agency_alias %>%
  filter(source == "njoaguof") %>%
  select(agency_county, agency_name, agency_id)

njoaguof::incident %>%
  filter(format(incident_date_1, "%Y") == "2024") %>%
  mutate(agency_county = as.character(agency_county)) %>%
  inner_join(uof_agency, by = c("agency_county", "agency_name")) %>%
  count(agency_id, name = "incidents") %>%
  inner_join(
    officer %>%
      filter(year == 2024) %>%
      count(agency_id, wt = officer_count, name = "officers"),
    by = "agency_id"
  ) %>%
  mutate(incidents_per_officer = incidents / officers) %>%
  left_join(agency %>% filter(first_year <= 2024, final_year >= 2024), by = "agency_id") %>%
  select(agency_name, incidents, officers, incidents_per_officer) %>%
  arrange(desc(incidents_per_officer))
```

## Notes
These are the ways in which this package differs from the source data.

### Agency identifiers and names
The source identifies agencies by county and name only. This package assigns each agency a
stable ```agency_id```, and records every spelling seen in ```agency_alias```. The
```agency_name``` in ```agency``` is the 2025 release's spelling, except for these
agencies, where it fixes a truncation or follows the "Twp PD" naming of the other agencies:
```{r}
agency_alias %>%
  filter(source == "njoag-leod-2025") %>%
  inner_join(agency, by = "agency_id", suffix = c("_source", "")) %>%
  filter(agency_name_source != agency_name) %>%
  select(source_name = agency_name_source, agency_name)
```

Agencies that the source lists as "State or Other Agency" have ```agency_county``` `NA`.

### Agency type and municipalities
The source no longer reports agency type. ```agency_type``` was assigned by this package,
starting from the 2021 release's agency types, with some corrections: for example, Chester PD
serves both Chester borough and Chester township, and the police departments of private
universities have type "Other". The municipalities in ```agency_municipality``` were also
assigned by this package, including municipalities served under shared-services agreements.
The sources for these are recorded in ```inst/extdata/agency_municipality.csv```.

### Incomplete agency reports
The data is as reported by each agency, and some agency-years look incomplete. For example,
Lakewood PD reports 153 officers in 2021 but 20 in 2022 and 58 in 2025, and Saddle Brook PD
reports about 30 officers every year until 2025, when it reports 5. This package does not
correct these. Here are the agency-years with fewer than half the agency's median number of
officers (among agencies with a median of at least 10). This is only a rough screen: it misses
agencies that report too few officers in most years, such as Fair Lawn PD, which reports 7 to
17 officers in 2021--2024 and 56 in 2025.
```{r}
officer %>%
  count(agency_id, year, wt = officer_count, name = "officers") %>%
  group_by(agency_id) %>%
  mutate(median_officers = median(officers)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(median_officers >= 10, officers < median_officers / 2) %>%
  left_join(agency, join_by(agency_id, between(year, first_year, final_year))) %>%
  select(year, agency_county, agency_name, officers, median_officers) %>%
  arrange(year, agency_county, agency_name) %>%
  print(n = Inf)
```

### Recoded values
"Not Provided" and "Blank" are recoded as `NA`, and yes/no answers as logicals. One value in
the source has a trailing space (`"Other "` as the reason for no appointment), which has been
removed.

## Installation

You can install the latest version of njoagleod from [GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("tor-gu/njoagleod")
```
